notes.example:
I'm a bit apprehensive about the biopsy results.
She felt apprehensive before her first day on the ward.
He was apprehensive about telling his consultant the news.
notes.synonyms: to have reservations about / to feel some anxiety about

notes.example:
I felt uneasy about the patient's reluctance to answer.
There was an uneasy silence in the meeting.
She grew uneasy as the symptoms worsened overnight.
notes.synonyms: to feel a sense of disquiet / to be ill at ease

notes.example:
The patient is anxious about the upcoming surgery.
I'm anxious that we might miss the deadline.
He became increasingly anxious while waiting for the scan.
notes.synonyms: to be deeply concerned / to be worried sick

notes.example:
The child was frightened by the loud machine.
She was frightened of needles as a young patient.
He looked frightened when the alarm went off.
notes.synonyms: to be alarmed / to be fearful

notes.example:
I was terrified when the car skidded on the ice.
She was terrified of the diagnosis being confirmed.
He stood terrified as the storm closed in.
notes.synonyms: to be extremely alarmed / to be gripped by terror

notes.example:
She was petrified of flying and avoided it for years.
I was absolutely petrified during the interview.
He stood petrified, unable to move a muscle.
notes.synonyms: to be paralysed with fear / to be utterly terrified
notes.register: potoczne · częste — swobodna rozmowa; nie w liście

notes.example:
Try not to panic if the pain returns suddenly.
She panicked when she couldn't find the referral letter.
The crowd began to panic as the exits filled up.
notes.synonyms: to be overcome by fear / to lose composure

notes.example:
Be wary of strangers offering unsolicited advice.
I'm wary of prescribing it without the full history.
She remained wary of his overly confident claims.
notes.synonyms: to be cautious of / to exercise caution regarding

notes.example:
Prescribing ten times the intended dose was an egregious error.
The report described an egregious abuse of power by the hospital board.
Falsifying the patient's notes was an egregious breach of trust.
notes.register: formalne · rzadkie — publicystyka i Reading C; do rozpoznawania

notes.example:
The sales representative's unctuous manner made the doctors suspicious.
He gave an unctuous speech praising the minister.
Her unctuous smile disappeared as soon as the cameras were switched off.
notes.register: formalne · rzadkie — ocena z dezaprobatą; do rozpoznawania

notes.example:
He's always sucking up to the consultant in the hope of a good reference.
I'm not going to suck up to the manager just to get better shifts.
She sucked up to the board members all evening.
notes.synonyms: to toady to / to curry favour with / to crawl to
notes.register: potoczne · częste — z dezaprobatą; rzeczownik suck-up raczej amerykański; nie w liście

notes.back: budzić obrzydzenie, przyprawiać o mdłości (także w sensie moralnym)
notes.example:
The smell from the infected wound turned my stomach.
The way they treated the staff turned my stomach.
Reading about the neglect of those patients really turns my stomach.
notes.synonyms: to make someone feel sick / to disgust
notes.register: codzienne · częste — mowa i publicystyka; nie w liście

notes.example:
The trial revealed the depravity of the doctor who harmed his patients.
Critics described the treatment of the prisoners as moral depravity.
The novel explores the depravity of life in Victorian London.
notes.register: formalne · rzadkie — kontekst moralny i prawniczy; do rozpoznawania
